title: Naturality of the explicit transported boundary of an injectively exact square
statement: Let C and an injectively exact square S of additive group-valued functors be as in [lem-sc-injectively-exact-square-resolution-short-exact], with its explicitly defined transported boundary b_S(F,n). First, for every morphism f:F->G and n>=0, R^n D(f) followed by b_S(G,n) equals b_S(F,n) followed by R^{n+1} A(f). Second, for every other such square T and every morphism of the underived squares tau:S->T, preserving their four edges, b_S(F,n) followed by R^{n+1} tau_A(F) equals R^n tau_D(F) followed by b_T(F,n). Both clauses refer to the same concrete boundary formula. No exactness assertion is included here.

proof.text: For the explicit boundary [lem-sc-injectively-exact-square-resolution-short-exact], For F -> G lift the morphism to the two chosen injective resolutions as in [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift]. Applying the four functors gives a morphism of the short exact sequences of complexes, with the middle map the pair of the B and C maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality] the transported connecting maps commute with the derived functor maps. This proves the object-variable naturality equality for this explicitly defined boundary. Homotopy independence identifies the maps with the canonical right derived functor maps and removes dependence on the lifted morphism. The same chosen resolution for a fixed F is used for every square.

For the explicit boundary [lem-sc-injectively-exact-square-resolution-short-exact], A morphism of the four underived functors preserving the four edges of the squares induces a morphism of their section-complex short exact sequences on the chosen resolution of every F. Its outer maps on homology are the components of the derived outer natural transformations (NatTrans.rightDerived_app_eq, in the same Mathlib RightDerived source as [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift]). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-long-exact-naturality] again and transport through the same comparisons. This yields delta_S followed by R^{n+1} tau_1 = R^n tau_4 followed by delta_T, simultaneously for all morphisms of squares.

lean.statement:
theorem boundary_naturality (S : InjectivelyExactSquare.{u, v, w} C) (n : ℕ) :
    (∀ {F G : C} (f : F ⟶ G),
      (S.X₄.rightDerived n).map f ≫ S.boundary G n =
        S.boundary F n ≫ (S.X₁.rightDerived (n + 1)).map f) ∧
    (∀ (T : InjectivelyExactSquare.{u, v, w} C) (φ : S.toSquare ⟶ T.toSquare) (F : C),
      S.boundary F n ≫ (NatTrans.rightDerived φ.τ₁ (n + 1)).app F =
        (NatTrans.rightDerived φ.τ₄ n).app F ≫ T.boundary F n)
